news.title: Argentina World Cup final bans reduced as FIFA approve request for suspension loophole
news.lede: FIFA has granted a request to reduce the duration of Argentina's punishment following their disgraceful conduct during the World Cup final. Leandro Paredes received a hefty 10-game ban for his post-match behaviour, which included kicking Eric Garcia and pushing Gavi to the ground as Spain celebrated their 1-0 win after extra-time. Paredes, 32, was also handed a £66,500 fine. Argentina stars Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada, along with coach Roberto Ayala, also received bans and fines.

news.title: Korean coach for Vietnam men's national football team eyes historic World Cup berth
news.lede: Kim Sang-sik, head coach of the Vietnam national football team, poses at the Vietnam Football Federation office in Hanoi, July 25. Korea Times photo by Heo Kyung-joo. Having coached Vietnam to their second straight Southeast Asian men's football title, Korean tactician Kim Sang-sik said Friday his ultimate goal is to take his team to the FIFA World Cup for the first time. Kim spoke with Korean media on Zoom on Friday, two days after Vietnam held off Thailand to win the ASEAN Hyundai Cup title.

news.title: FIFA approve Argentina FA's request to REDUCE bans for World Cup final chaos
news.lede: FIFA have approved a request to reduce Argentina's punishment for their disgusting behaviour at the World Cup final . Midfielder Leandro Paredes received a whopping 10-match ban for his post-match antics, which included kicking out at Eric Garcia and shoving Gavi to the ground as winners Spain celebrated their 1-0 victory after extra-time . Paredes, 32, was also handed a £66,500 fine. Team-mates Nahuel Molina and Thiago Almada as well as coach Roberto Ayala also received bans and fines.

news.title: Herrington reveals call from icon to soothe World Cup pain
news.lede: Updated August 28, 2026 - 5.00am. First published at 4.40am. Lucas Herrington has revealed that Zlatan Ibrahimović called him to double down on his support after Australia’s heartbreaking World Cup exit on penalties. Herrington, 18, bravely stepped up to take a Socceroos spot kick against Egypt in the round of 32 match in Dallas in July.

news.title: Argentina hit with sanctions for Falklands banner, World Cup final brawl
news.lede: Argentina have been hit with major sanctions by Fifa over their display of a Falkland Islands banner, while two players face lengthy bans for their actions in the World Cup final. After beating England 2-1 in their Fifa World Cup semi-final, Argentina players paraded a banner that read “Las Malvinas son Argentinas”, which translates to the Falklands belong to Argentina. Three EPL players, including Manchester United’s Lisandro Martinez and former Tottenham Hotspurs players Cristian Romero and Giovani Lo Celso, were pictured with the banner. The rivalry between the two nations over the islands was a hot topic before the match, with the tension being traced back to the South American nation’s invasion of the Falklands in 1982.

news.title: UEFA to bring criminal complaint against Infantino
news.lede: European football’s governing body said it is preparing a criminal complaint against the FIFA president over his failed plan to sell a stake in the World Cup. Just a day after UEFA reportedly agreed to remove their threat of boycotting FIFA tournaments, European football's governing body has launched a new wave of pressure on FIFA President Gianni Infantino to resign. UEFA has asked a US federal court for permission to obtain testimony and documents about the creation of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) subsidiary. FFE was Infantino's plan to sell a stake in FIFA's commercial rights linked to ‌men's ​and women's World Cups and the Club World Cup.

news.title: Uefa prepares criminal case against Fifa president Gianni Infantino over World Cup sell off plan
news.lede: Uefa is preparing to launch criminal proceedings against Fifa president Gianni Infantino over his botched attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup. European football's governing body has applied for the release of documents related to Infantino's Fifa Forward Enterprise plan which involved seeking private investment in the World Cup and its other tournaments. Uefa alleges Infantino developed the proposal in secret with a small group of advisers and investors, bypassing the normal governance processes of world football's governing body and failing to consult Fifa's Council, regional confederations or member associations.

news.title: Fifa reduce Argentina players' punishments for disgraceful World Cup final antics including Leandro Paredes punch-up
news.lede: FIFA have reduced the punishments for Argentina’s disgraceful World Cup final antics. Thug Leandro Paredes was slapped with a TEN-match ban and fined £66,500 for his shocking behaviour at the end. Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and coach Roberto Ayala also received bans and fines. Molina got a seven-match ban, Almada one and Ayala three.
